findings.title: limitFunction no longer forwards call arguments
findings.cause: index.js:121-124 now returns `() => limit(() => function_())`, so every invocation drops `...arguments_` before calling the wrapped function.
findings.impact: Any limited function that expects parameters now receives `undefined` values, breaking documented and benchmarked use cases such as `limitedFetchUrl(url)` and `limitedTask(delay, i)`.
findings.evidence: Source mismatch across index.js:121-124, index.d.ts:133-136, recipes.md:144-164, and benchmark.js:193-194. Direct probe `limitFunction(async (a, b) => [a, b], {concurrency: 1})('x', 'y')` produced `[undefined, undefined]` (JSON serialized as `[null, null]`). test.js:343-356 only checks concurrency, so this regression is currently untested.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run `node --input-type=module` and evaluate `import {limitFunction} from './index.js'; const limited = limitFunction(async (a, b) => [a, b], {concurrency: 1}); console.log(await limited('x', 'y'));`.

findings.title: Options-object construction silently enables rejectOnClear by default
findings.cause: index.js:6-7 changed the destructuring default from `rejectOnClear = false` to `rejectOnClear = true` whenever callers pass `{concurrency: ...}`.
findings.impact: Consumers using the documented `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` form opt into `AbortError` rejections on `clearQueue()` without asking for them, which changes shutdown/teardown semantics and can surface unexpected rejections in existing code.
findings.evidence: The public contract in index.d.ts:99-106 and readme.md:46-57 documents `rejectOnClear` with default `false`. A focused runtime probe created one running and one pending task with `pLimit({concurrency: 1})`, called `clearQueue()`, and observed the pending promise reject immediately with `{name: 'AbortError', message: 'This operation was aborted'}` instead of remaining pending. test.js covers `rejectOnClear: true` at 199-215, but not the default behavior for the options-object path.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run `node --input-type=module` and evaluate `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1}); const running = limit(() => delay(40)); const pending = limit(() => 'done'); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue(); console.log(await Promise.race([pending.then(v => ({status: 'resolved', v}), e => ({status: 'rejected', name: e.name})), delay(0).then(() => ({status: 'pending'}))])); await running;`.

findings.title: limit.map stops passing indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: index.js:107-112 now gates the mapper index on `Array.isArray(iterable)`, so Sets, iterators, and other valid iterables receive `undefined` instead of their position.
findings.impact: Mapper logic that depends on the documented `(value, index)` contract breaks for non-array iterables even though the API still advertises full iterable support.
findings.evidence: index.d.ts:30-43 and readme.md:78-85 say `limit.map(iterable, mapperFunction)` passes both item and index for an `Iterable`. The current runtime returns `['missing', 'missing']` for `await limit.map(new Set(['a', 'b']), async (_value, index) => index ?? 'missing')`. test.js:239-254 checks value handling for Set and iterator inputs but never asserts index propagation, so the regression slips through.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run `node --input-type=module` and evaluate `const limit = pLimit(2); console.log(await limit.map(new Set(['a', 'b']), async (_value, index) => index ?? 'missing'));`.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass runtime validation
findings.cause: index.js:12 changed the guard to `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`, which skips validation for falsy invalid values like `0`, `''`, or `null`.
findings.impact: JavaScript callers can pass invalid configuration without getting the documented type error, and the library silently falls back to `false` semantics instead of surfacing misconfiguration.
findings.evidence: The option type remains `rejectOnClear?: boolean` in index.d.ts:99-106. A direct probe `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})` completed without throwing, even though the previous runtime guard in the checked-out diff rejected any non-boolean. test.js has no runtime coverage for falsy invalid values, and index.test-d.ts:28-29 only catches the truthy string case at type-check time.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run `node --input-type=module` and evaluate `import pLimit from './index.js'; try { pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0}); console.log('accepted'); } catch (error) { console.log(error); }`.

commands_run: rg -n "Infinity|POSITIVE_INFINITY|rejectOnClear|limitFunction\(|map\(|concurrency" benchmark.js recipes.md readme.md index.d.ts test.js index.js
